Subject: MPO: repurchase window + multi-buyer gating workflow

Hi Jake / Procurement team, Emily —

Quick one: BrightWave is looking to convert the 90-day pilot credits into a 12–18 month private offer (MPO) and the buyer mentioned they may repurchase additional seat bundles across two business units. Before we put the offer together, can you confirm two things: 1) the repurchase/activation window for a private offer if the buyer intends to onboard additional AWS accounts under the same MPO, and 2) whether multi-buyer gating (different BU admins signing) will require separate approvals per AWS account or can be consolidated under a single signer?

I attached a short renewal request that BrightWave emailed earlier (BrightWave_Renewal_REQ.pdf) and an initial terms spreadsheet (MPO_Term_Summary.xlsx) — both attached as stubs. We're trying to avoid a situation where the buyer signs a 12-month MPO and later needs separate approvals for each account, which would slow activation. Emily — is there a standard flow on the AWS side for linking accounts to a single private offer activation? Any timing constraints we should bake into the mutual action plan?

Proposed next step: if you can share the finance approver (CFO or procurement lead) we can draft a DocuSign with explicit account mappings and proposed term (12 vs 24 months) to avoid re-approval.

Thanks,
Lukas Meyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lukas.meyer@redwood.ai

Attachments: BrightWave_Renewal_REQ.pdf (application/pdf, stub), MPO_Term_Summary.xlsx (spreadsheet, stub)

Lukas — thanks for the clear note. Short answer: yes, but there are caveats.

On Wed, Nov 4, 2026 at 9:12 AM Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick one: BrightWave is looking to convert the 90-day pilot credits into a 12–18 month private offer (MPO) and the buyer mentioned they may repurchase additional seat bundles across two business units. Before we put the offer together, can you confirm two things: 1) the repurchase/activation window for a private offer if the buyer intends to onboard additional AWS accounts under the same MPO, and 2) whether multi-buyer gating (different BU admins signing) will require separate approvals per AWS account or can be consolidated under a single signer?

What we recommend: create the MPO with explicit account IDs listed in the private offer activation. If the buyer expects to add accounts later, include a clause that allows up to N additional account mappings within X days of signing (we usually see 30–90 days). If accounts are added after that window, procurement will require an amendment which is an extra manual approval.

Multi-buyer gating depends on the "buyer identity" rules. If the buyer wants separate BU-level approvers to sign, we can set the MPO to accept signatures from a set of email domains (e.g., @brightwave.com) and enable centralized activation by an org admin — that avoids per-account signoffs. However, if they require separate CFO-level approvals per BU, that becomes a procurement policy at the buyer and will force separate procurement reviews on our side.

Timing: allow 7–10 business days for AWS Marketplace processing once the DocuSign is complete and accounts are validated. If you want a faster activation (2–3 business days) we can request expedited review but will need the buyer's finance contact and a clear account mapping in the DocuSign.

I can draft the recommended DocuSign template and share a DocuSign link — please confirm who the primary signer will be and whether you want the 30- or 90-day add-account window.

Best,
Emily Barnes
Principal Partner Rep, AWS Marketplace
emily@amazon.com

Thanks Emily — that's helpful. Adding a couple of product/finance constraints from our side so we can be explicit in the MPO: 

- Pricing/term recommendation: recommend standard 12-month MPO with an optional 12-month extension clause. For customers splitting spend across business units, we often propose a 12-month committed core + usage overage billing per account so that the committed discount applies company-wide while allowing incremental seat purchases per BU.
- Co-sell credits: if BrightWave wants co-sell incentives, we should lock in the partner referral structure before signature; otherwise co-sell eligibility can be applied retroactively but that's slower.
- Activation gating: prefer the 90-day add-account window for enterprise customers that have multi-BU rollouts. It reduces chance of amendment requests.

Lukas — can you confirm whether BrightWave's procurement will accept a single CFO signature for the entire MPO (and whether that CFO can delegate activation to BU admins)? If yes, Emily's centralized activation approach is ideal. If not, we'll need to schedule a brief sync with their procurement/finance leads and include an approval matrix in the MPO.

I'll draft the pricing language in MPO_Term_Summary.xlsx and mark the cells that change depending on 12 vs 24 month terms.

-Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
